clue.text: Coach universally accepted by this opera singer

parts.note: a coach is a railway carriage, a car
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone
so, as in 'do it so', means in this way

explanation.surface: A singer travels on a coach that everyone happily accepts.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema rating for films anyone may see, hence 'universally accepted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Caruso was the famous Italian operatic tenor.

clue.text: Pen name's last used for complaint in The Observer?

parts.note: a pen for pigs is a sty

indicators.note: the last of the word name's is its final letter

explanation.surface: A columnist's pseudonym is used to lodge a grievance in a Sunday newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday paper, but here it is the eye, the organ that observes; the complaint is an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A small inflamed swelling on the eyelid is an ailment of the organ that does the observing.

clue.text: Innovative business eschewing husband's artwork

indicators.note: eschewing means avoiding, so a letter is kept out

parts.note: innovative means new or fresh
CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: A pioneering firm does without the husband's painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eschewing' removes the H from FRESHCO.
explanation.definitionFit: A mural painted onto wet plaster is a classic kind of artwork.

clue.text: Did a short sketch of academic sending up food shop

parts.note: a prof is an academic, a professor

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending up means reading the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

explanation.surface: Someone sketched a professor who mocked a grocery store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending up' looks like mockery but turns DELI into ILED.
explanation.definitionFit: To write a brief biographical portrait of someone is to give a short sketch of them.

clue.text: Wonderful cast showing effort, but missing Oscar

parts.note: to heave is to throw with effort

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'
Oscar is O in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A wonderful cast of actors put in effort, though one Oscar eluded them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing Oscar' takes O out of ONLY, leaving NLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly is used informally for delightful or divine, a synonym of wonderful.

clue.text: Nothing originally conceived by politician works

parts.note: FA is short for 'sweet FA', British slang for nothing at all

indicators.note: originally means at its start, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician claims to have come up with a scheme from nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet FA' is British slang for nothing; 'works' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A works is a manufacturing plant, the same as a mill or plant.

clue.text: Hunted down Chaka Khan's earliest recordings in Rough Trade

indicators.note: in places the initials inside the shuffled letters
rough means crude or unrefined, so the letters are knocked into a new order
earliest picks the opening letter of each name

explanation.surface: Someone hunted down Chaka Khan's first recordings on the Rough Trade record label.
explanation.walkthrough: Rough Trade is a real British record label, but 'Rough' is the anagram signal; 'recordings' only completes the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To track someone is to follow their trail and find them.

clue.text: That woman trains on in hundred degree shade

indicators.note: in places the run of pieces inside the outer letters

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
that woman is her
RY is short for railway, the trains
re means on or about

explanation.surface: A woman goes training in hundred-degree heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hundred degree' looks like a temperature but splits into two single letters that wrap the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep bright red colour is a shade, a tint of colour.

clue.text: Field marshal briefly keeps combat gear in NAAFI?

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so one piece goes inside another
briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Lord Kitchener was a British field marshal
combat is war

explanation.surface: A senior officer keeps combat equipment in the forces canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: The NAAFI is the British armed forces' canteen and shop service, so its gear would be pots and pans.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots, pans and utensils are what a canteen kitchen uses, its gear.

clue.text: Part of Faye Dunaway's back fully exposed

indicators.note: back means read in the opposite direction
part of means a section is taken from within the words

explanation.surface: A section of the actress Faye Dunaway's back was on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' lifts EDUN out of 'Faye Dunaway's'; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked means wholly uncovered, completely exposed.

clue.text: After it's over, females like a strong drink

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: F is short for female; FF is the plural

explanation.surface: When it's all finished, women fancy a strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses IT'S to STI.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff drink is a strong one, potent with alcohol.

clue.text: Hollow victory on points for green-eyed monster

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north

indicators.note: hollow means emptied, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: An empty win on points brings out jealousy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' are compass directions, not a scoring method.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Othello calls jealousy the green-eyed monster, and covetousness is its twin.

clue.text: Fats no good for performing tenor

indicators.note: no means without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Placido Domingo is a performing tenor

explanation.surface: A fat person is no good as a stand-in for a tenor on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fats' looks like a plural noun but is the first name of rock'n'roll pianist Fats Domino.
explanation.definitionFit: Fats was the nickname of the New Orleans singer and pianist, so the surname completes it.

clue.text: Confusion caused by fuel gauge initially round motorway northwards

indicators.note: in a down clue, northwards means read from bottom to top

parts.note: oil is a fuel

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

parts.note: an orb is a round object
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: Muddle arises from a fuel gauge reading around the motorway heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northwards' turns the whole string OILGORBMI upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangled, embarrassing muddle or complicated situation is a state of confusion.

clue.text: Her coin assortment includes pound that's added to the pool?

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so one piece goes inside
an assortment is a mixture, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: L is short for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A woman's mixed coins include a pound she puts into the kitty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pool' suggests a betting pot of money, but it is a swimming pool; 'assortment' rearranges HER COIN to CHORINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemical disinfectant is dosed into swimming water to keep it clean.

clue.text: Rat created system of banks westwards

indicators.note: in an across clue, westwards means read from right to left

parts.note: BACS is the UK interbank automated payments system

explanation.surface: A traitor set up a network of banks heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: BACS is the British banks' automated clearing system for payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is a strikebreaker, someone who works on while others strike.

clue.text: Native American and Tibetan perhaps discussing the universe

indicators.note: discussing means talking, so what is heard counts, not spelling

parts.note: a Cree is a Native American; a Tibetan is an example of an Asian

explanation.surface: Two people from different cultures talk about the cosmos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Tibetan as one example of an Asian.
explanation.definitionFit: Everything that was made, the whole cosmos, is called the created world.

clue.text: Fake cobbler, say, nails shoe vacuously

indicators.note: nails means pins or holds fast, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a cobbler is a fruit pudding, so an example of a pud

indicators.note: vacuously means emptily, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A sham shoemaker hammers nails into a shoe without thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cobbler' suggests a shoemaker but is a baked fruit dessert, and pud is British slang for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseud is a pretentious poser, someone fake about their learning.

clue.text: One describes trip to station with wit

parts.note: a post is a station, a place of duty
a card is a wit or joker

explanation.surface: Someone recounts a witty journey to a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' is a holiday: a picture card sent home describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday card mailed home typically tells friends about the journey.

clue.text: Audibly demolish fish

indicators.note: audibly means by sound, so what is heard counts, not spelling

parts.note: to raze is to demolish

explanation.surface: Fish are noisily destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Skates and stingrays are flat cartilaginous fish.

clue.text: Woodworker's gear used to be not at all secure, looking back

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: was means used to be
no means not at all
to net is to secure or catch

explanation.surface: A carpenter's equipment once felt insecure in hindsight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' reverses WASNONET as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fine-toothed saw for cutting joints is part of a carpenter's kit.

clue.text: Unexpected shiner covers side of eye having confronted dukes

indicators.note: covers means goes round, so one piece is wrapped by another

parts.note: the sun is something that shines

indicators.note: having confronted means standing in front of, so one piece follows another

parts.note: D is short for duke; DD the plural

indicators.note: a side of a word is its edge, here the first letter

explanation.surface: A black eye appears after a fistfight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shiner' and 'dukes' (fists) suggest a fight, but the shiner is the sun and dukes are DD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrupt and unforeseen happens without warning.

clue.text: There's a loud protest, as wife's stuck in middle of Ormskirk

indicators.note: stuck in means placed inside something
the middle of a word is its central letters

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of
W is short for wife; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A spouse complains noisily while trapped in a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ormskirk is a market town in Lancashire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A squawk is a loud harsh complaint, an outcry.

clue.text: Ten soldiers trapped inside hospital section surviving

indicators.note: trapped inside means held within

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
X is the Roman numeral ten
the TA is the Territorial Army, British reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Ten soldiers caught in a hospital ward have survived.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still in existence has survived.

clue.text: Heavy music hacking off master and others

indicators.note: hacking off means cutting away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: metal is heavy rock music

explanation.surface: Loud rock music irritates the master and the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacking off' looks like annoying but means cutting away.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation means and the rest, used after a list of names.

clue.text: Start of Channel Four broadcast somewhere in the Med

indicators.note: start of means the first letter
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Channel 4 opens its broadcast from a Mediterranean location.
explanation.walkthrough: Channel Four is a British TV channel; 'broadcast' rearranges FOUR to ORFU.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek island lies in the Ionian Sea, part of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Encountered unknown European city

parts.note: met means encountered
Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone met a stranger in a city on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city stands on the Moselle in Lorraine.

clue.text: Demure eaters both essentially silent

indicators.note: essentially means at the core, so the middle letters of each of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Modest diners both keep quiet at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable or unwilling to speak means making no sound.

clue.text: Dwell for a time in London area, preferring joint to heroin regularly current

indicators.note: preferring one thing to another means swapping it in
to links the preferred thing with the one it replaces

parts.note: Soho is a district of central London
H is slang for heroin
J is slang for a joint of cannabis

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: Stay in a London district, choosing cannabis over hard drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preferring joint to heroin' swaps H for J in SOHO; 'regularly' takes URN from 'current'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sojourn is a temporary stay, a short time living somewhere.

clue.text: Child aged twelve months receives wide style of shoe?

indicators.note: receives means takes in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a tot is a small child
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
a baby aged twelve months is one year old

explanation.surface: A year-old toddler is given a broad shoe style.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, scored W.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoes made in two contrasting colours, like brogues or spectators, are a recognised style.
